title: The program it writes, and the design at its end
summary: One .rex file is both the program and the design. It holds: a UserDialog subclass whose defineDialog makes the controls with createXxx and connects events with connectXxxEvent; one UNGUARDED accessor per control (self~lcd~setText(x)); one method per event named on_<control>_<event> holding the user's code (the form's OK and CANCEL override ok and cancel); the form's variables as ::attribute; the form's own methods; generated helpers (<tab>_pageChanged, <tab>_show, timer_<t>, and for bound dialogs <ctl>_bound, <list>_load/_save/_add/_remove); ::routines; ::RESOURCE strings.<language> when translatable; and last ::RESOURCE oodDesign, the design as lines (form, control, prop, event, binding ...). Open... reads the design back from the resource and the event code from the methods. v0.16 kinds: UPDOWN (props min max pos buddy opts tip; setBuddy in initDialog, never AUTOBUDDY by default; with SETBUDDYINT the buddy's _data starts at pos), MONTHCALENDAR (opts tip; SELECT and SELCHANGE: startDate, endDate, id, hwnd). Every visual kind has a tip prop: one ToolTip per dialog (id = highest control id + 1) and tips~addTool(self~ctl, text) in initDialog; key <control>.tip with languages, only for a control with a tip. TRACKBAR events DRAG and ENDTRACK (info, hwnd) via connectTrackBarEvent. v0.17: form line resizable=1 (written only when set); then the class inherits ResizingAdmin, the create style gains THICKFRAME, and ::method defineSizing has defaultSizing(STATIONARY LEFT, STATIONARY TOP, MYLEFT LEFT, MYTOP TOP) plus controlSizing(id, left, top, right, bottom) for each control whose anchor prop is not LEFT TOP (or that is on a tab page: pinned to the tab's id; tabs first). anchor is LEFT TOP RIGHT BOTTOM words in that order, CENTER for none, "" (older designs) read as LEFT TOP. An anchored axis edge pair stretches (STATIONARY both); one edge moves (STATIONARY that edge, MY* the other); none follows the centre (STATIONARY XCENTER/YCENTER). v0.18: the CATCH/FINALLY guard at the top of a program is, for each word used: signal on syntax name oodKnows<WORD>; oodProbe = .Routine~new("oodProbe", "catch syntax" or "finally"); call errorDialog ...; return 1; oodKnows<WORD>: -- an ooRexx that knows the word refuses the lone clause at compile time (10.8, 10.12); one that does not compiles it as a command. It replaced 'if .RexxInfo~revision < 13514' (a build from git answers r0). MONTHCALENDAR default size 150x110 DU.
invariants: Round trip is byte-identical: generate, read back, generate again gives the same file (t01, t03, t10 check it).
Whatever lies between the last event method and the next directive is read back as that method's code: a generated ::routine keeps its comment inside the routine, never before it.
Generated code uses only documented upstream ooDialog API so it runs on Windows ooDialog unchanged.
Every generated method is UNGUARDED, as the ooDialog guide asks of event handlers.
Background events reply at once (after EXPOSE, which must come first).

A trace probe is a message on its statement's own line: .OodTraceProbe~step(where, node, thread, .context~variables); the step answers RESULT as it was. Never a CALL: a CALL sets SIGL and drops RESULT, so a traced run would see other values than an untraced one. t02 runs the same code both ways and compares.

CATCH needs ooRexx r13514 or later; FINALLY is in no ooRexx yet (2026-11-15). An older ooRexx reads both words as commands and runs every clause, so: a program whose code has a CATCH clause starts with a guard (if .RexxInfo~revision < 13514 then errorDialog and return 1), and the designer refuses Run and Trace for CATCH before r13514 and for FINALLY on any ooRexx (OodDesign~catchWords, catchRefusal; found from the text). When FINALLY lands, catchRefusal and the guard need its revision.

A DO, LOOP or SELECT's CATCH and FINALLY clauses are graph nodes of kind catch/finally in the block's "catch" slot, each with a body; an empty DO body takes inserts before its first CATCH. Inserted blocks keep their shape: END, CATCH, FINALLY at the first line's level.
Event code takes its own arguments with use arg: the generator writes the method header, not use arg. The arguments are in the catalogue's evargs lines.
Do not name a Rexx variable b (or x) when it follows a closing quote in a concatenation: "..."b is a binary string literal (a syntax error at load). Seen in v0.17's generateSizing.
Never decide what an ooRexx can do from .RexxInfo~revision: a build from github.com/ooRexx/ooRexx answers 0. Ask it (compile a probe); nothing need be run.

provenance.claim: The model, catalogue, generator and reader.
